text.agentsmd.budget_none: No budget limit is set; still keep costs low.
text.agentsmd.rule_service: service — runs continuously; over budget, the operator is asked instead of stopping it.
text.agentsmd.rule_session: session — sleeps after %d idle minutes; your next call wakes it automatically.
text.llms.a2a: POST %s/a2a speaks A2A JSON-RPC 2.0 (protocol 0.3; tasks/send and tasks/sendSubscribe are accepted as aliases). Send a text part with the command plus metadata.box_id (or a data part {box_id, command}) to run it as an async job — the task id is the job id; send a data part {"tool": "box_up", "arguments": {...}} to call any tool. message/stream returns SSE status/artifact updates until the task is completed, failed or canceled.
text.llms.auth: Send `Authorization: Bearer <key>` to %s/v1 and /mcp. Agent keys (bx_agent_…) only see their own boxes; admin keys see everything. Create boxes with `Idempotency-Key` to make retries safe.
text.llms.choose:
- Do not guess sizes: pass a `profile` (below) to box_ensure or box_up and Boxaz picks template, CPU/RAM, lifecycle and placement.
- Unsure, or got NO_CAPACITY? Call box_recommend: it ranks the warm pool (pre-started container, ~1 s), a container on a pool host, an Incus VM (own kernel) and new provider servers by a 0-100 score with price, ETA and reasons, and lists rejected options with why.
- Hard limits go in requirements: max_price_hour, max_latency_ms + location (region, country code or lat,lon), isolation (container | vm | sandbox), arch, region. Soft preference: optimize = balanced | cost | speed | reliability | latency.
- Untrusted code: profile sandbox-untrusted (VM, offline by default). 24/7 bots and webhooks: long-running-service. Repo work: coding-agent. Scraping: browser-automation.
- Every create response has estimate {kind, cost_per_hour, expected_total_usd, eta_seconds, actual_seconds, warm_hit}. Errors include next: suggested tool calls.
- Reuse instead of re-creating: box_ensure(name) returns the same box (woken, with a resume summary); box_clone copies a live box in milliseconds on copy-on-write storage.
text.llms.sandbox:
- Besides VPS hosts, Boxaz runs boxes in per-second sandbox APIs. box_recommend shows them as kind `sandbox` with price, boot time and capabilities (fork, pause, ports, max lifetime); short tasks, untrusted code and fast starts favour them.
- T2: Boxaz starts its agent inside the sandbox, so every tool works. T3: an exec-only shim at the gateway (no terminal, snapshots or egress rules).
- GET /v1/sandbox/providers lists each adapter with its verification level (live-verified, docs-verified, sdk-source).
text.llms.concepts:
- Lifecycle: task (auto-terminated at TTL), session (sleeps when idle, wakes on the next call), service (always on).
- Exec returns exit_code, stdout_tail/stderr_tail (last 60 lines), truncated, log_id, files_changed, tokens_saved and `next` hints. Long commands: async=true + GET /v1/jobs/{id}?wait=30.
- Snapshots keep /work and /memory; restore rolls a box back, fork starts a new box from a snapshot.
- Budgets: per box (budget_usd), per agent per day/month, and global. POST /v1/quote prices a spec without creating anything.

text.llms.details: Every box has /work (your files) and /memory (shared notes for the agent). Command output is trimmed to the last lines to save tokens; full logs are one call away. Errors carry a stable code, a one-sentence hint, and optional retry_after_s; send Accept-Language: vi|en|zh|ja to localize them.
text.llms.errors_intro: Envelope: {"error": {"code", "message", "hint", "retry_after_s"?, "docs_url"?}}. The code never changes with the language.
text.llms.qs1: Get an agent key (bx_agent_…) from the operator and export it as BOXAZ_API_KEY.
text.llms.qs3: Call box_ensure(name, profile) to get-or-create your box (box_recommend shows ranked options first; box_quote prices an explicit spec).
text.llms.qs4: Use box_write / box_exec / box_exec_batch, read full output with box_logs, and finish with box_down.
text.llms.summary: Boxaz rents cheap, disposable Linux sandboxes (boxes) to AI agents on low-cost VPS providers, picks the cheapest host that fits, sleeps idle boxes and enforces budgets.
text.mcp.instructions: Boxaz gives you disposable Linux boxes. Typical flow: box_ensure(name, profile) (or box_recommend → box_up) → box_write/box_exec (box_exec_batch for several commands) → box_down. Output is trimmed to save tokens; read full logs with box_logs only when needed. Snapshot before risky changes; box_restore undoes, box_fork branches. Files are also readable as resources (boxaz://box/{id}/file/{path}). Web apps: box_app_set runs and supervises a server; box_url gives its stable Boxaz URL (wakes a sleeping box); box_url_token makes it private (the provider's own preview URL, if any, stays reachable for anyone who knows the sandbox id). Humans reach the box beyond HTTP: box_forward (localhost port → a TCP port in the box, e.g. Postgres), box_ssh_info (ssh / VS Code Remote-SSH with no sshd in the box), box_ticket (single-use ticket for the terminal / tcp / ssh WebSockets; never put an API key in a URL), box_terminal_sessions (durable terminal sessions).

text.prompt.cost-review.desc: List boxes and spend, then sleep or delete what is not needed.
text.prompt.cost-review.text: Review my Boxaz spend: call box_cost (overall), then box_list. For each running box show slug, lifecycle, cost_per_hour and spent_usd (box_cost with box_id). Propose: box_sleep for idle session boxes, box_down for finished task boxes (snapshot first if it has unsaved work). Ask before deleting anything, then report the expected savings per day.
text.prompt.cost-review.title: Review Boxaz spend
text.prompt.debug-failing-command.desc: Reproduce a failing command in a box, read the full log, find the cause, fix it and verify.
text.prompt.debug-failing-command.text:
In Boxaz box %s the command `%s` fails. Debug it step by step:
1. box_snapshot the box so you can roll back.
2. Run the command with box_exec (tail_lines 80). If it is truncated or fails, read the full output with box_logs(log_id, tail_lines=300).
3. Inspect the relevant files with box_read / box_grep and the environment (versions, env vars, cwd /work).
4. State the root cause in one sentence, apply the smallest fix with box_write or box_exec, and re-run the command until exit_code is 0.
5. If the fix made things worse, box_restore the snapshot. Summarize the cause, the fix and the final output.
text.prompt.debug-failing-command.title: Debug a failing command
text.prompt.start-project.desc: Price, create and set up a box for a goal, then build and verify it.
text.prompt.start-project.text:
Goal: %s
Use Boxaz with template %s:
1. box_templates to confirm the template, then box_quote (lifecycle session) and tell me the cost_per_hour.
2. box_up with a short slug and an idempotency_key.
3. Write the code with box_write under /work, install dependencies and run it with box_exec_batch (stop_on_error true).
4. Keep notes for later runs in /memory/NOTES.md.
5. box_snapshot when it works, report the result and the spend (box_cost), then box_sleep the box (or box_down if nothing is left to do).
text.prompt.start-project.title: Start a project in a new box

text.llms.h_apps: Web apps, Boxaz URLs and tokens (v1.7)
text.llms.apps:
- Run long-lived servers with box_app_set {start, port, repo?, install?, ready_http?}: Boxaz clones, installs once, starts the app, restarts it on crash with backoff, starts it again after wake / restore / clone and holds traffic until it is ready. Watch it with box_app_status and box_app_logs (GET /v1/boxes/{id}/app/logs?follow=1 streams SSE). Prefer this over `nohup … &`.
- Every exposed port has gateway_url, a stable Boxaz URL (box_url): the first request to a sleeping box wakes it (wake_on_request, on by default; PATCH /v1/boxes/{id}), WebSocket and SSE pass through unbuffered.
- Share privately with box_url_token: an expiring, revocable token for one box+port (`?token=`, `Authorization: Bearer` or `X-Boxaz-Token`); the port switches to access=token. Caveat: the token protects only the Boxaz URL. With a gateway domain or an internet-facing BOXAZ_PUBLIC_URL, E2B and Novita sandboxes are created private: their preview host answers 403 without the sandbox traffic token, which only the gateway adds, and the port reports provider_preview=private. Where a port reports provider_preview=public (Daytona, or BOXAZ_PROVIDER_PREVIEW=public) the provider preview URL stays reachable by anyone who knows the sandbox id; do not rely on the token for secrets there.
- GET /v1/capabilities lists per provider: memory_pause, wake_on_http_native, wake_via_gateway, fork, inbound_http, max_runtime.
- GET /v1/gateway shows the gateway domain, URL pattern (https://<name>.<domain>/), reserved subdomains and the provider-preview policy.
- URLs are readable (v1.9): https://<name>.<domain>/ serves the box's primary port (the app port, else the first port) and https://<name>-<label>.<domain>/ the other ports (label = web, api, db, … never a number). The name comes from subdomain / name / slug at creation; rename with box_url {name} or PATCH /v1/boxes/{id} {subdomain}, label a port with box_url {port, label}. The older <key>-<port> address stays as alias_url. Name URLs are guessable: use box_url_token for private apps.
text.llms.h_access: Box access: terminal, port forward, SSH (v1.10)
text.llms.access:
- Humans reach a box beyond HTTP with single-use access tickets: POST /v1/boxes/{id}/tickets {purpose: terminal|tcp|ssh, port?, session_id?, ttl_s?} → `bxa_…`, redeemable once within 60 s, bound to one box and purpose; revoking it (DELETE /v1/boxes/{id}/tickets/{tid}, `all` = every ticket) closes the sessions using it. The terminal / tcp / ssh WebSockets take `?ticket=` or an `Authorization` header — never an API key in the URL, never a cookie — and browsers must come from an allowed origin (BOXAZ_DASHBOARD_URL, BOXAZ_ACCESS_ORIGINS).
- Durable terminal: wss://<core>/v1/boxes/{id}/terminal?ticket=…&proto=2&mode=control|view[&session=…] (or wss://<name>.<domain>/.boxaz/terminal). Sessions survive disconnects for BOXAZ_TERMINAL_DETACH_TTL (10 min) and replay the last 256 KiB on reattach; one controller, many viewers. List / kill: GET / DELETE /v1/boxes/{id}/terminals[/{sid}]. proto=2: output in binary frames, JSON control frames (session, viewers, control, exit, ping; send resize, control, ping).
- Port forward: `box forward <box> <port> [local]` (MCP box_forward) streams a localhost port to a TCP port in the box over wss://<name>.<domain>/.boxaz/tcp?port=N; allowed ports = exposed ports + POST /v1/boxes/{id}/forward-ports (PATCH forward_ports to replace).
- SSH without sshd in the box: `box ssh <box> [-- cmd]`, `box ssh-config --write` (ProxyCommand `box ssh-proxy %h`), VS Code / Cursor Remote-SSH, `ssh -L`, sftp. Keys: GET/POST/DELETE /v1/ssh/keys; host key: GET /v1/ssh; summary per box: GET /v1/boxes/{id}/access.
